metadata.title: PISA 2000: Sample Weight Problems in Austria

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The paper addresses PISA 2000 Austria sample weight problems arising from inadequate coverage of vocational students in combined school-and-work-based programmes. It explains that PISA country scores are computed as weighted means of student values, where weights are intended to reflect the proportions of strata in the target population. Using supplementary stratum-by-gender student counts from the Austrian Ministry of Education, the author constructs corrected weight schemes (“pop2000” and “sample2003”) by rescaling weights within each stratum-by-gender cell. For subsequent analyses consistent with standard PISA practice, the paper notes that BRR replicate weights (80 BRR variables) should be adjusted according to the corrected weights; however, the working paper itself primarily demonstrates the impact of the corrected weights on country mean scores and plausible-value distributions rather than re-estimating full model-based results.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The paper does not describe any missing-data handling procedure because it focuses on correcting sampling/stratification weights and examining how those corrections change weighted country means and the distribution of PISA plausible values. Since the analysis is centered on reweighting and visualization of plausible-value distributions rather than reporting an explicit missing-data imputation/deletion strategy, the missing-data handling is not documented in the provided text. This is therefore treated as a reporting gap for missing-data procedures, not as evidence that missingness was absent.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic focus is Austria’s PISA 2000 assessment. The paper does not report a further student-level inclusion/exclusion filter beyond the PISA sampling/stratification design; instead, it corrects the weighting to address misrepresentation of a vocational stratum in the target population. It also discusses joining two strata with very low weights in PISA 2000 (AHSdiv and BSlf) when constructing the corrected weighting schemes.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education Working Paper examines how Austria’s PISA 2000 results are biased due to inadequate coverage of students in combined school-and-work-based vocational programmes, relative to PISA technical standards. The paper explains that PISA country scores are computed as weighted means across 19 school-type strata, and that the sum and distribution of weights should match the target population. It shows implausible changes in total weights from PISA 2000 to PISA 2003 (about +21%) and large stratum-percentage differences, especially for the BS tech/gew (BStg) stratum, which is associated with gender composition and achievement differences. Using Austrian Ministry of Education school statistics, the author constructs corrected weights (“pop2000”) and demonstrates that applying them to PISA 2000 lowers country mean scores versus the original weights (e.g., Reading 507.1 → 492.1; Mathematics 515.0 → 502.5; Science 518.6 → 504.7). The paper recommends using the corrected weights for more reliable longitudinal comparisons and notes that BRR replicate weights should be adjusted accordingly for standard PISA analyses.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a methodological/technical working paper focused on sampling weight correction for PISA 2000 Austria rather than on training and evaluating machine-learning models. As such, there are no predictive ML targets, no reported ML performance metrics, and no fabricated main findings table entries. The paper also does not provide an explicit analytic-sample N or per-country student counts in the excerpt, because its core contribution is the construction and demonstration of corrected weighting schemes and their impact on weighted plausible-value distributions and country means.
